messages:
Olivia Chen: Heads-up — deploy-bot blocked the canary for chart v2.14.0 because values-configmap checksum changed and we're inside the 10pm-6am change window. https://ci.example.com/job/12345 :eyes:
Kevin Park: I saw that. The configmap change is a small feature flag flip from the data team, but it touches the feature toggle config used by the gateway. Deploy-bot left: `change-window-exemption-required`
Olivia Chen: Data team says it's low risk and they'd like to ship tonight due to customer impact. We need a plan: either pin to v2.13.2, apply a values override that keeps old toggle, or get an exception.
Jen Ortiz: Quick question — does v2.13.2 have any incompatible CRD changes? Last I checked it's just the configmap keys.
Alex Rivera: No CRD changes. v2.13.2 -> v2.14.0 only touches configmap + small template tweak. Safe to pin for now.
Olivia Chen: OK. Option A = pin chart to 2.13.2 and reopen canary, Option B = manual canary outside window with 2 approvals + SRE Oncall standby, Option C = values-hotfix keeping toggle=false and roll. Thoughts?
SRE Oncall: If we do manual canary outside window we need runbook + rollback steps + oncall + 2 approvers. I'm available. Prefer pin to reduce blast radius.
Maya (release-manager): We also need release notes updated and the jira ticket annotated. If pinning, we should schedule a follow-up to reintroduce the change in the next day change window. I'll own communication.
Kevin Park: I'm leaning pin. Quick command to pin in helmfile/values: `chart: repo/redwood-gateway
version: 2.13.2` — then push commit, let deploy-bot pick it up.
Olivia Chen: If someone wants to hotfix instead, this is the values override to keep old toggle:
```yaml
gateway:
  featureFlags:
    experimentalX: false
```
(replace in overlays/prod/overrides.yaml)
Jen Ortiz: If we pin, what is rollback plan if pin causes regression?
Alex Rivera: Rollback plan: 1) monitor canary for 15m, if errors spike >3% revert to v2.14.0 by reverting the commit and let deploy-bot redeploy; 2) run `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=gateway -o wide` to inspect; 3) if KV cache issues, scale replicas to 0 and back to force cold start. Documented in runbook link: https://wiki.example.com/runbooks/gateway-rollback
Deploy Bot: auto-check: canary paused due to policy: change-window; awaiting commit with version pin or manual-exempt tag.
Olivia Chen: Action items: Kevin will open PR to pin to 2.13.2, include follow-up ticket to reapply the configmap change in next window; Maya will update release notes and jira; SRE Oncall will standby for 30m after canary resumes.
Kevin Park: Opening PR now: https://git.example.com/r/redwood/infra/merge/987 — includes commit message "pin gateway chart to v2.13.2 to avoid change-window risk"
Deploy Bot: detected PR 987, running preflight checks: lint ok, values-schema ok, no image digest drift. Scheduling canary start in 2m.
SRE Oncall: Canary started. Observability links: traces: https://trace.example.com/q/abc, dashboard: https://dash.example.com/gateway-canary. I'll call out if errors >3%.
Olivia Chen: Thanks — if anything abnormal call me and Maya. Otherwise we'll merge and ship pinned version and write postmortem items next week. :thumbsup:
Maya (release-manager): Note added to jira: "Pinned gateway chart to v2.13.2 to mitigate change-window risk for configmap. Follow-up: re-evaluate feature flag rollout and schedule for next window."
Kevin Park: Merge complete, deploy-bot resumed canary and rolled out to 5% traffic.
Deploy Bot: canary health: healthy (5m), promoted to 20% traffic per policy.
SRE Oncall: Canary looks clean for 20m, no error spike. Recommend full rollout.
Olivia Chen: Merging to main release channel. Thanks team.
Kevin Park: After-action note: we'll add a CI hook to detect configmap-key changes and auto-tag change-window-risk in PR description to avoid surprise blocks.
